symptom: The documented classification path states that every constraint is typed by a two-stage pipeline: a metric stage followed by a signature stage that may override it. Reading the canonical entry point confirms this — both stages run on every call. Three specific constraints never reach that entry point at all.
mechanism_as_described: A separate module adds clauses to the lookup predicate that the canonical path consults first. For three hardcoded historical constraints those clauses match and return a type directly, so the pipeline is never entered; some of them call a first-stage helper internally and thus receive metric typing with no signature stage at all. The clauses predate the two-stage architecture and were written to validate specific scenarios. Nothing in the code or the documentation marks them as an exception, so a reader who checks the canonical path — which is correct — concludes the invariant holds universally, and the check confirms exactly what it was pointed at.
detection_path: A structured verification pass that enumerated every module against the claimed invariants rather than reading the canonical path and confirming it.
consequence: Three constraints carry types produced by a different procedure than the one the architecture documents, with no marker at either the code or the document level. The divergence produces no error and no differing output shape.

extraction_notes.alternatives_not_extracted: The same file reports a second defect: a stage-9 module mutates the config database at runtime (restoring afterwards), which violates the single-source-of-truth boundary although the specific parameter is not read by the classifier, so its current effect is zero. One unit per directory is the rule; the bypass was chosen as the more incident-shaped of the two. Recorded so the choice is auditable rather than invisible.
extraction_notes.unit_is_incident_not_audit: The unit describes the defect the audit found, not the audit.
